partner_context.their_ambition: As the Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore you steward the world's busiest transshipment port and are driving it toward a clean-energy future — mandating that all new harbour craft from 2030 be fully electric, B100-capable or net-zero-fuel ready, with net-zero harbour craft by 2050.
partner_context.their_pressure: Singapore is landlocked for land transport yet ringed by water, and you are investing proactively in efficient transport infrastructure. Your electrification mandate needs credible, fast, exportable clean-vessel options — not just slower battery retrofits.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier makes electric the fast, premium, exportable option: a software-defined foiling standard you can prove first-of-class at home and export as a Singapore-led benchmark — including a fast East Coast↔CBD line for a city short on road capacity.

hero.title: Singapore MPA × Navier — the foiling standard for a clean harbour-craft future
hero.subtitle: Singapore has already mandated cleaner harbour craft. Navier makes the electric option the fast, premium, exportable one.
hero.what_we_do_together: We make Singapore the proving ground and global reference for software-defined foiling vessels. Navier's Pioneer II runs zero-emission across the harbour and inner waterfront; Quanta-LR's hybrid range opens the cross-border crossings the region already makes by slow ferry. MPA gets a first-of-class clean-harbour-craft showcase, a decarbonization path, and a home-grown standard to export.

why_now: MPA's harbour-craft electrification targets give explicit top-cover for a clean-vessel transition, and Singapore is the busiest port and one of the densest waterfront cities on earth. Foiling makes electric viable at speed — efficient per passenger-mile, smooth, near-silent — with no charging-infrastructure dependency for the long cross-border legs. A ~100-vessel Navier network is already ramping in the Maldives (2026).

objections.response: Foiling cuts energy per passenger-mile dramatically, so electric range and speed both work — making the 2030 mandate practical rather than a compromise on performance.

objections.concern: Charging infrastructure in a dense port?
objections.response: Pioneer II charges at existing terminals on a pedestal; Quanta-LR's hybrid range covers the cross-border legs with no new infrastructure.
Software-defined controls and a clear first-of-class path — and Singapore is the ideal jurisdiction to set the exportable standard.

objections.concern: Wake and safety in one of the world's busiest ports?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed: geofenced low-wake and no-foil zones in anchorages and fairways, automatic speed limits, and full pilotage compliance. The vessel foils only on cleared corridors — and a foiling hull throws far less wake at speed than today's planing craft.

the_ask.partner_brings: You bring clean-craft berth access, the 2030 mandate cover, MRT/bus integration and the regulatory platform to set the standard.

close.title: The clean harbour-craft standard — proven in Singapore, exported to the world.
close.body: From a harbour pilot to a full waterfront network to the cross-border Riau corridor, Navier gives MPA the fast, zero-emission, exportable standard that its harbour-craft transition is reaching for.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
